title: Protocol to Identify Covalent Inhibitors Targeting RhoA Cys16
author: Koo, Ho, et al.
materials: RhoA Pull-down Activation Assay Biochem Kit

steps.title: Obtain GST‑tag plasmids
steps.instruction: Retrieve pGEX‑containing plasmids from Addgene: pGEX‑2T‑RhoA‑wt (Addgene #12959), pGEX‑2T‑Cdc42‑wt (Addgene #12969), and pGEX‑2T‑Rac1‑wt (Addgene #12977).

steps.title: Express GST‑tag proteins in BL21(DE3)
steps.instruction: Transform each plasmid into E. coli BL21(DE3), grow in LB + ampicillin (100 µg/mL) at 37 °C for 16–18 h; inoculate 4 mL of this culture into 1 L TB + ampicillin (100 µg/mL) and incubate at 37 °C for 4–5 h until OD₆₀₀≈0.6 (monitor after 2.5 h); induce with 0.1 mM IPTG and shift to 18 °C for 16–18 h (typical IPTG range 0.1–1 mM, induction 12–16 h).

substeps.instruction: Transform plasmids into BL21(DE3) and culture in LB with 100 µg/mL ampicillin at 37 °C for 16–18 h.
Transfer 4 mL starter culture to 1 L TB containing 100 µg/mL ampicillin; grow at 37 °C for 4–5 h until OD₆₀₀≈0.6.
Add 0.1 mM IPTG, incubate at 18 °C for 16–18 h.

steps.title: Purify GST‑tag proteins via glutathione beads
steps.instruction: Harvest cells (4 000 × g, 4 °C, 20 min), resuspend pellet in 5 mL B‑PER™ Complete Bacterial Protein Extraction Reagent per gram pellet plus protease inhibitor cocktail (1 tablet/10 mL); vortex vigorously, clarify (16 000 × g, 4 °C, 30 min); incubate lysate with pre‑equilibrated glutathione‑agarose beads (bead:lysate ratio 1:10) for 1 h at 4 °C with gentle rotation; wash beads 5–7 times (700 × g, 4 °C, 3 min each wash, monitor supernatant Abs₂₈₀ until zero/negative); elute with fresh elution buffer, pellet beads (3 000 × g, 4 °C, 3 min), collect eluate, repeat if needed; measure protein concentration with Nanodrop and check Abs₂₆₀/₂₈₀ (~0.6).

substeps.instruction: Harvest bacterial pellet by centrifugation at 4 000 × g, 4 °C, 20 min.
Add 5 mL B‑PER™ reagent per gram pellet with protease inhibitor (1 tablet/10 mL); vortex vigorously.
Clarify lysate by centrifugation at 16 000 × g, 4 °C, 30 min; keep supernatant.
Incubate supernatant with glutathione‑agarose beads (1:10 bead:lysate) for 1 h at 4 °C with gentle rotation.
Wash beads 5–7 times with washing buffer (pellet 700 × g, 4 °C, 3 min each); monitor supernatant Abs₂₈₀ until zero/negative.
Elute proteins with freshly prepared elution buffer, pellet beads at 3 000 × g, 4 °C, 3 min, collect eluate; repeat if necessary.
Measure protein concentration with Nanodrop; verify Abs₂₆₀/₂₈₀ ≈0.6.

steps.title: Dialyze proteins to remove glutathione
steps.instruction: Pre‑wet a 7 kDa MWCO dialysis cassette with PBS or exchange buffer, load protein sample, incubate cassette in PBS with stirring at 4 °C for 1 h; replace PBS every hour, then continue dialysis in fresh PBS for 16–18 h; collect dialyzed protein with a syringe and quantify (Bradford, BCA, or Lowry).

substeps.instruction: Pre‑wet 7 kDa MWCO dialysis cassette with PBS or exchange buffer.
Load protein sample into cassette.
Stir cassette in PBS at 4 °C for 1 h; replace PBS each hour.
Incubate in fresh PBS at 4 °C for 16–18 h.
Collect dialyzed protein using a syringe.
Quantify protein amount (Bradford, BCA, or Lowry assay).

steps.title: Assess protein purity by SDS‑PAGE
steps.instruction: Aliquot 30 µg of each protein, boil in reducing sample buffer for 5 min, resolve by gel electrophoresis, and visualize bands with Coomassie blue or silver stain; expect a single ~47 kDa band.

substeps.instruction: Aliquot 30 µg protein, denature by boiling in reducing sample buffer for 5 min.
Run samples on SDS‑PAGE.
Stain gel with Coomassie blue or silver stain; verify single ~47 kDa band.

steps.title: Obtain RhoGEF/RhoGAP plasmids
steps.instruction: Retrieve the following Addgene plasmids: pEGFP‑FLAG‑AKAP‑Lbc (Addgene #67571), pDEST‑EGFP_Hu_p115‑RhoGEF (WT) (Addgene #136337), pCAG‑mCherry‑FKBP‑GAP (Addgene #222632), and pEGFP‑SRGAP1 (Addgene #1187269).

steps.title: Seed HEK293T cells
steps.instruction: Plate HEK293T cells in a 10‑cm dish and incubate 16–18 h at 37 °C, 5 % CO₂ to reach ~50‑60 % confluency for transfection.

steps.title: Transfect HEK293T cells
steps.instruction: Prepare DNA‑lipid mixture: Tube A – 60 µg plasmid DNA in 500 µL Opti‑MEM; Tube B – 60 µL Lipofectamine 2000 in 500 µL Opti‑MEM; incubate each 10 min at 20‑25 °C; combine tubes, mix gently (no vortex), incubate 20 min at 20‑25 °C; add dropwise to cells and incubate 48 h at 37 °C, 5 % CO₂ (monitor GFP/RFP expression).

substeps.instruction: Prepare Tube A: 60 µg DNA in 500 µL Opti‑MEM.
Prepare Tube B: 60 µL Lipofectamine 2000 in 500 µL Opti‑MEM.
Incubate each tube 10 min at 20‑25 °C.
Add Tube B to Tube A, mix slowly (no vortex).
Incubate mixture 20 min at 20‑25 °C.
Add mixture dropwise to cells; incubate 48 h at 37 °C, 5 % CO₂.

steps.title: Harvest cell lysates
steps.instruction: Aspirate medium, wash cells twice with pre‑chilled PBS, scrape cells into exchange buffer, probe‑sonicate 15 s at 15 % power, centrifuge lysate at 13 200 × g for 5 min, keep supernatant, determine protein concentration (Bradford/BCA/Lowry) and normalize samples.

substeps.instruction: Aspirate culture medium.
Wash cells twice with pre‑chilled PBS.
Scrape cells into exchange buffer.
Probe‑sonicate suspension 15 s at 15 % power.
Centrifuge at 13 200 × g, 5 min; collect supernatant.
Quantify protein concentration and normalize.

steps.title: Synthesize compound 1a
steps.instruction: Add furfural (1 equiv) and 2‑acetylbenzofuran (1 equiv) to sodium hydroxide (1.25 equiv) in ethanol/water (1:1); allow reaction to complete, then extract and purify the organic product.

steps.title: Form hydrazine intermediate
steps.instruction: Add hydrazine (2.0 equiv) to compound 1a in ethanol and heat under reflux; extract the organic intermediate and proceed without further purification. Handle hydrazine in a certified fume hood with appropriate PPE.

steps.title: Acylate to produce CL16
steps.instruction: Add chloroacetyl chloride (1.2 equiv) and triethylamine (2.0 equiv) in dichloromethane to the refluxed mixture on ice; stir for 16 h, then extract and purify to obtain CL16. Handle chloroacetyl chloride with caution in a fume hood.

steps.title: Synthesize compound 1b
steps.instruction: Repeat the step for compound 1a but substitute 2‑acetyl‑7‑hydroxybenzofuran for 2‑acetylbenzofuran, using the same equivalents and solvent conditions.

steps.title: Alkylate to produce compound 2b
steps.instruction: Add propargyl bromide (1.5 equiv) and potassium carbonate (2.5 equiv) to compound 1b (1.0 equiv) in acetonitrile; extract and purify the organic product to yield compound 2b.

steps.title: Synthesize CL16‑alkyne
steps.instruction: Follow the procedures of steps 2 (hydrazine addition) and 3 (acylation) using compound 2b in place of compound 1a to generate CL16‑alkyne.

description: Ras homolog family member A (RhoA) is a cellular small GTPase that governs proliferative signals and cytoskeletal dynamics. It is often upregulated in malignancies, such as breast, gastric and colorectal cancers (CRC), and hence is considered a therapeutic hotspot in oncology. However, due to its smooth surface and globular structure, RhoA has long been classified as an “undruggable” target. To address this challenge, covalent targeting of a unique cysteine on RhoA by covalent inhibitors, that generally exhibit stronger binding with the protein targets, could be an effective strategy. Recently, we identified that RhoA Cys16 is the unique cysteine in RhoA subfamily and is absent in other Rho GTPases. Notably, Cys16 is located adjacent to the functional domains (nucleotide-binding pocket and switch regions) of RhoA, suggesting the feasibility of modulating RhoA activity through small molecule binding to Cys16. We have developed a covalent inhibitor, CL16, targeting RhoA Cys16 in CRC cells. It significantly inhibits RhoA activity, leading to promising anti-cancer and anti-metastatic effects in CRC cells and mouse CRC models. This protocol below describes the steps for identifying covalent inhibitors targeting RhoA Cys16 in CRC. It consists of: (1) Gel-based ABPP coupled with covalent ligand screening to identify lead compounds with specific binding to RhoA in vitro; (2) Mass spectrometry experiments to confirm RhoA Cys16 as the binding site of the lead compounds; (3) Molecular experiments to study the effects of the compounds on RhoA interactions with RhoGEF or RhoGAP expressed in CRC cells; (4) Cellular experiment to study the RhoA inhibitory effects of the compounds; (5) Mouse CRC xenograft models to assess antitumor effects of the lead compounds in vivo. This protocol focuses on the identification of RhoA covalent inhibitors. Detecting and characterizing such inhibitors is crucial to decipher the activities and mechanisms of action of these synthetic compounds. Thes
